subject.title: [Feature]: Auto-discovery of agent configurations from external workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw core support trusted external-workspace agent config discovery, or should multi-project setups use explicit `agents.create/update/delete` plus hot config reload and optional plugin/docs conventions?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested scanner crosses config, trust, session routing, and live Gateway lifecycle boundaries that repository policy leaves to maintainer product/security judgment.

options.title: Design trusted discovery first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define trusted roots, file format, precedence, reload/removal behavior, diagnostics, and security constraints before implementation.

options.title: Prefer explicit hot management
options.body: Close or narrow scanner work and invest in `agents.create/update/delete`, CLI, and Gateway hot reload so operators can add agents without external config scanning.

options.title: Move to extension convention
options.body: Keep core lean by documenting a plugin or workspace convention for external tooling to generate central `agents.list` entries without making runtime scan arbitrary workspaces.

recommendation.title: Design trusted discovery first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define trusted roots, file format, precedence, reload/removal behavior, diagnostics, and security constraints before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest history signal around multi-agent config/routing and the agent-list management boundary.
